summary: This paper establishes a unified dynamical regime map for finite-length transmission lines capacitively coupled to transmon qubits, showing that the appropriate description—continuum reservoir, discrete multimode coupler, or single-mode resonator—is selected by the hierarchy among the qubit frequency $\omega_q$, transmission line characteristic frequency $\omega_{\mathrm{TL}} = 2\pi v_p/d$, and coupling characteristic frequency $\omega_g = 2\pi/(Z_{\mathrm{TL}}C_s)$. Using hierarchical equations of motion and symmetry-resolved decomposition into even/odd parity sectors, the authors characterize memory effects, non-Markovianity via the Breuer–Laine–Piilo measure, and the validity of perturbative approximations across all three regimes.
motivation: Finite transmission lines in superconducting circuits play qualitatively different physical roles depending on operating parameters, yet no unified framework has clarified when a continuum, multimode, or single-mode description applies, nor when Markovian approximations remain valid.
method: Starting from circuit quantization using the auxiliary-mode representation, the authors derive a Hamiltonian where transmission line modes separate into even and odd parity sectors coupled via collective qubit operators $L_\pm = \sigma_y^{(1)} \pm \sigma_y^{(2)}$. They solve the full reduced dynamics non-perturbatively using HEOM and compare with secular GKLS and time-convolutionless master equations.
result: In the long-line continuum limit ($\omega_{\mathrm{TL}} \ll \omega_g, \omega_q$), each parity sector exhibits Drude–Lorentz spectral density $J(\omega) = 2\lambda\gamma\omega/(\gamma^2 + \omega^2)$ with $\gamma \approx \omega_g/(2\pi)$; the comb-edge discrete region ($\omega_{\mathrm{TL}} \ll \omega_g$, $\omega_q \lesssim \omega_{\mathrm{TL}}$) requires explicit multimode treatment; in the short-line limit ($\omega_g \ll \omega_{\mathrm{TL}}$), a single isolated mode dominates with coupling $g_n \propto 1/n$.
